task: DAEO-0z8c (W2-05) fix batch: make the lexical index's read-only git calls (W2-108's freshness calls among them) run pinned, so `gov close`'s planted case (W2-M161, R6-2) goes green.
status: DONE. The sandbox check passed. The planted `gov close` case is green and so are W2-108's acceptance cases. Two cases of `test_w2_05_planted.py` are red here, the retrieval-check cases. They are just as red with the fix taken out, and the check itself hangs in this sandbox (see unresolved).
work_completed: In `src/gov/retrieval/lexical.py`, `_git` now calls `git_env(root, pinned=True)` instead of `git_env(root)`, with a two-line comment. That one change covers all four calls the index makes: `_tracked`'s `ls-files -z` and `hash-object --stdin-paths`, and W2-108's `_tree`'s `rev-parse HEAD --git-path index` and `ls-files -z`. All four only read. Pinned, they no longer read the system or global git configuration, so a trace setting there is never written to. I did not change `_checked`'s logic or W2-108's key. On `hash-object`: it has no `-w`, so it only reads, and I pinned it too. Left unpinned, it would still write the person's trace file on every refresh or freshness check that hashes, and the KPI would not be met. Pinned, the repository's own `.gitattributes`, `.git/info/attributes` and `.git/config` still apply. I probed it (script in my temporary folder): for an ordinary project the blob ids are the same pinned and unpinned, and a global trace setting changes nothing. The one difference is a person whose global configuration has `core.autocrlf = true` and who has a CRLF file in the working tree: unpinned, that file's id was the LF one (`422c2b7ab3b3`); pinned, it is the file as it stands (`c30dea8a3641`). These blob ids are used only inside the index, for change detection and chunk ids; nothing compares them with git's own index. The effect is that the id no longer depends on who runs it, and a store built under such a configuration shows that file stale once, after which the next refresh re-indexes it. I wrote three builder tests first and saw two of them red. Sweep row 24 and the counts paragraph are updated.

discoveries: In this sandbox, `python3 -m gov.retrieval.retrieve_check` run in the worktree printed nothing and was killed by `timeout 300` (exit 124). The sandbox reported outbound connections to `ollama.com:443` refused. This fits the two retrieval-check cases being red here with or without the fix. I read no failure text, so the cause inside the cases is not confirmed.
risks: A person whose global configuration has `core.autocrlf = true`, working with CRLF files, will see those files stale once and re-indexed at their next refresh, because the blob ids now follow the file as it stands and the repository's own settings. Nothing else uses these ids.
lessons: A git call added later to a module that already has a `_git` helper inherits that helper's environment, so W2-108's new calls came in unpinned. Sweep rows naming a helper should be re-checked when a merge brings new callers of it.
